production.note: US model years 2024-2026. Start: 2024 model (The Drive's '2024 Chevy Corvette E-Ray' first drive; KBB, Sean Tucker, 17 Jan 2023: 'The E-Ray goes on sale in 2023', kbb-e-ray-news-2023). End year is provisional: Cars.com lists a 2026 Corvette E-Ray with '655 @ 6450' (carscom-e-ray-2026), and chevrolet.com's Corvette page (chevrolet-corvette-lineup-2027, at the /e-ray address) now lists Stingray, Grand Sport, Grand Sport X ('721 Combined horsepower'), Z06, ZR1 and ZR1X, with no E-Ray. No GM statement that the E-Ray ended with 2026 was found.

body.note: KBB: offered as a coupe (from $104,295) and a convertible (from $111,295). The coupe has a removable roof panel; the convertible is a retractable hardtop sold under the same E-Ray name.

configuration.note: '6.2-liter V8 with a front single-motor electric drive unit'

displacementL.note: '6.2-liter V8' (LT2). The cc figure was not on a page opened for this car.

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated 6.2-liter LT2 V8 (no forced induction mentioned).

fuel.note: Full hybrid, not plug-in: '1.9-kWh lithium-ion battery' with a front electric motor.

drivetrain.note: '8-speed dual-clutch automatic | all-wheel drive'; KBB: 'The electric motor powers the front wheels. The V8 powers the rear set.'

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL: publications (combined system output). The Drive spec box (Peter Holderith, 13 Oct 2023), quote: "655 (495 from V8 @ 6,450 rpm | 160 from electric motor)". KBB editorial (kbb-e-ray-news-2023, Sean Tucker): "a total of 655 horsepower". Cars.com: 'SAE Net Horsepower @ RPM 655 @ 6450' (carscom-e-ray-2024). No Chevrolet page could be opened (news.chevrolet.com URL not found; corvetteactioncenter.com refused).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: publications reporting Chevrolet's DRY weight (weight-order step 4), standard coupe, 2024 model. The Drive spec box, quote: "Dry Weight | 3,774 pounds (coupe) | 3,856 pounds (convertible)". Carscoops (carscoops-e-ray-2023, Chris Chilton, 17 Jan 2023): "The E-Ray coupe's dry weight as 3,774 lbs (1,712 kg)". Cars.com labels it 'Base Curb Weight 3,774 lbs' (carscom-e-ray-2024), but it is the same Chevrolet dry figure. No Chevrolet curb weight was found; a real curb weight is higher (Carscoops: 'almost certainly going to top 4,000 lbs').

provisionalNote: Power (655 hp) and the dry weight (3,774 lb, coupe) rest on publications reporting Chevrolet's figures (The Drive's spec box, Carscoops, KBB editorial); a Chevrolet press release or specification table (news.chevrolet.com, or a GM release reproduced on corvetteactioncenter.com or vette-vues.com) would replace them, and a Chevrolet curb weight would replace the dry figure. The last model year (2026) is inferred from Cars.com and chevrolet.com's current lineup; a GM statement would replace it.
